description:
ApeLogic está conformado por estudiantes del 6.º semestre de Ingeniería de Sistemas e Informática de la Universidad Continental, uniendo talento de Ilo (Moquegua) y Arequipa. Buscamos desarrollar soluciones de alto impacto representando a la sede de Moquegua en el NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Áreas de enfoque:

Desarrollo de Software, Web (UI/UX) y Simulación.

Ciencia de Datos, IA y Machine Learning.

Hardware y prototipado.

Trabajamos con metodologías ágiles y rigor analítico.
summary: When a crewmate feels unwell far from Earth, numbers alone are not enough. ApeLogic is a local AI health copilot that helps astronauts record measurements, understand changes and access clear guidance during long-duration missions. Its assistant, ORI, combines onboard records with a searchable reference library and a locally hosted language model to explain relevant health information in plain language. An interactive 3D body connects indicators with body systems, while local history and trends make changes easier to follow. Guided measurement instructions explain how to obtain readings and why they matter. A dedicated emergency pathway supports urgent situations with structured guidance. NASA Human Research Program resources inform the space-health context; real historical OSD-575 data and NASA DONKI space-weather events provide complementary scientific context. Built by six Systems Engineering students at Universidad Continental, Peru, ApeLogic brings together local AI, understandable information and an interface designed around crew autonomy. Measure. Understand. Act.
details:
APELOGIC HEALTH COPILOT

THE PROBLEM

During deep-space missions, communication delays make immediate medical support from Earth difficult. Crew members need clear instructions to measure their health, understand changes and recognize when to ask for help.

OUR SOLUTION

ApeLogic combines ORI, a local AI companion, with an interactive 3D body and a persistent health record. The working prototype supports English and Spanish.

HOW THE CREW USES IT

1. Follow the measurement guide and manually log a reading, its time and context.

2. Select a body system to review related readings and trends.

3. Ask ORI about a symptom or recorded value. ORI retrieves local reference material and explains relevant records with sources.

4. For urgent symptoms, open the structured emergency walkthrough and follow the onboard mission protocol.

PROTOTYPE SCREENSHOTS

View the real prototype screenshots: https://github.com/JoosX/HackatonNasa/tree/DavidMAC/docs/img: panel overview, ORI conversation, measurement guide and urgent walkthrough. Screenshots use demonstration readings. The prototype requires clinical and mission-specific validation before operational use.

WHY LOCAL AI MATTERS

ORI brings the crew member's question, related records and reference information together. The onboard configuration uses Ollama with Gemma 3 4B and nomic-embed-text. The hosted demo also offers an optional online Gemini engine. Fixed urgent guidance remains separate from generated conversation.

NASA RESOURCES IN THE APPLICATION

- NASA HRP: spaceflight health risks inform the explanatory library.

- OSD-575: real Inspiration4 laboratory observations before and after flight provide historical research context, including a glucose visualization. They remain separate from current user records.

- NASA DONKI: cached space-weather events provide environmental context, not an astronaut's measured radiation dose.

ENGINEERING AND VERIFICATION

HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Three.js power the interface. Python/FastAPI serves the application, and SQLite stores records locally. Manual entries cover pulse, blood pressure, oxygen, glucose, temperature, sleep, mood and stress.

At source snapshot e5e62ae, verification on November 15, 2026 produced 156 passing Python tests and 13 passing JavaScript tests. Five Python checks were skipped because local AI or speech dependencies were unavailable. These are software checks, not clinical outcomes.

TRY THE PROJECT

- Live application: https://hackatonnasa-vwm1.onrender.com/

- PPT PITCH : https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sn8UZrmc-O39ojLhvO0dYo-6hA3d6lOX/view?usp=sharing

- Source and local setup: https://github.com/JoosX/HackatonNasa/tree/DavidMAC

- English architecture: https://www.figma.com/design/N5PDDT4Jj5VDmioCsgIYpd/ApeLogic-Health-Copilot-Architecture?node-id=0-1

- Video demo: https://youtu.be/ULoyiavoi5g

TEAM AND CREATIVE CREDITS

Six Systems Engineering students at Universidad Continental, Peru, developed ApeLogic. Claude and OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted development, research, writing and translation. AI tools also supported presentation illustrations and synthetic narration. External resources are listed in the submission references and repository.
